description: Quantitative Assessments of Native Fish Recovery in the San Juan River Basin is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USFWS, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. Construction of the Navajo Dam on the San Juan River in 1962, while necessary for water development and flood control in the area, has reduced native fish habitat through flow alterations. Coverage: San Juan River (2022). The toolkit gives San Juan River as the location, 2022 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
